claims.summary: The export returns the sum of all natural numbers below the input, reduced to 32 bits.
claims.reason: It covers every 32-bit input as an unsigned value and returns the sum of all smaller naturals modulo 2³², as intended.
claims.name: Examples.Toy.sumTo
claims.intent: `sum_to(n)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: `0 + 1 + … + (n − 1)`, wrapped to 32 bits.
details: Covers every 32-bit input, interpreted as an unsigned natural number for the range length.
The natural-number sum is converted to 32 bits, so the returned value is the sum modulo 2³².
Returns additionally guarantees that the module can be instantiated and every call terminates without trapping under every host behavior.
caveats: The range and sum are defined mathematically over natural numbers; the exported function must still finish for every 32-bit input, including inputs whose range is extremely large.

claims.summary: The export returns the lower bound when the input is below it, the upper bound when the input is above it, and otherwise the input.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Toy.Lifted.module "clamp"
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 hi]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (if x.slt lo = true then lo else if hi.slt x = true then hi else x)]
claims.reason: It compares inputs as signed 32-bit values and returns the lower bound, upper bound, or input according to the stated conditions.
claims.name: Examples.Toy.clamp
claims.intent: `clamp(x, lo, hi)` on signed 32-bit ints: `lo` below `lo`, `hi` above `hi`, else `x`.
details: The input values are compared as signed 32-bit integers, while the selected value is returned unchanged as a 32-bit bit pattern.
There is no arithmetic here that can wrap around.
Returns additionally guarantees that the module can be instantiated and every call terminates without trapping under every host behavior.
caveats: The comparisons are signed, but the selected result is the original 32-bit value; it is not converted to a mathematical integer.
No requirement says the lower bound must be less than or equal to the upper bound; the nested comparisons determine the result even when bounds are reversed.

claims.summary: The export returns the greatest common divisor of the two inputs interpreted as unsigned 32-bit values.
claims.statement:
∀ (a b : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Toy.Lifted.module "gcd" [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 a, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 b]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (BitVec.ofNat 32 (a.toNat.gcd b.toNat))]
claims.reason: It returns the greatest common divisor of both inputs interpreted as unsigned 32-bit values; that result fits in 32 bits.
claims.name: Examples.Toy.gcd
claims.intent: `gcd(a, b)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: their greatest common divisor (`gcd(a, 0) = a`).
details: Covers every pair of 32-bit inputs, each interpreted as an unsigned natural number.
The natural-number greatest common divisor is converted to 32 bits; this conversion would wrap modulo 2³², though the greatest common divisor here fits in range.
Returns additionally guarantees that the module can be instantiated and every call terminates without trapping under every host behavior.
caveats: The inputs are treated as unsigned magnitudes, not signed integers; values whose top bit is set are not negative for this calculation.
The greatest common divisor fits in 32 bits, so reducing the result to 32 bits does not change it.
